claims.text: Elemental distribution and surface segregation govern the formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Elemental distribution and surface segregation govern the catalytic performance of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Controlling synthesis temperature, pressure, and precursor ratios can optimize elemental distribution and surface segregation.
Elemental distribution and surface segregation act synergistically on catalytic active sites.
Optimized elemental distribution and surface segregation improve catalytic performance relative to conventional noble metal-based catalysts.
The hypothesis applies only to synthesis conditions and elemental compositions that permit formation of high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Non-optimized materials performing as well as or better than optimized materials would falsify the proposed relationship.
